evidence.quote: Many FOMC participants judge that the case for somewhat more accommodative policy has strengthened.
We will closely monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook and will act as appropriate to sustain the expansion.
Inflation is expected to return to 2 percent over time, but at a somewhat slower pace than we foresaw earlier in the year.
However, the risks to this favorable baseline outlook appear to have grown.
the limited available evidence we have suggests that investment by businesses has slowed from the pace earlier in the year.
The question my colleagues and I are grappling with is whether these uncertainties will continue to weigh on the outlook and thus call for additional policy accommodation.

parsed.rationale: The speech signals a shift from patience toward possible easing, stressing grown downside risks from trade and global growth and slower-than-expected inflation. A caution against overreacting to data tempers it only slightly.
